description: Flexbox is used to design responsive layouts in React Native across different screen sizes.

justifyContent.description: Aligns children along the main axis.

alignItems.description: Aligns children along the cross axis.
alignItems.note: Stretch works only when child has no fixed size in that dimension.

alignSelf.description: Overrides alignItems for a single child.

flex.description: Defines how items fill available space along the main axis.

flexGrow.description: Controls how extra space is distributed. Accepts any floating point number.

flexShrink.description: Controls how items shrink when overflowing.

flexBasis.description: Default size of an item before grow/shrink calculations.

gap.description: Spacing between both rows and columns.

position.note: absolute takes the element out of the flow.

zIndex.description: Stacking order of the element. Higher numbers are on top.

direction.description: Layout direction for text and children.

Containing Block.description: Determines the reference frame for absolute positioning.

Flex Basis vs Width/Height.description: flexBasis takes precedence over width (in row) or height (in column) if both are set.

bestPractices: Use flex: 1 instead of fixed dimensions for responsive containers.
Prefer inline styles or StyleSheet for performance.
Combine justifyContent and alignItems to center content easily.
Use useWindowDimensions() hook for layout calculations if flex isn't enough.
